view.title: LLM Generator: Horizon Europe Data Management Plan
view.help: Uses a language model to generate a draft data management plan for a Horizon Europe project based on information provided in the RDMO project. Generation may take some time.
view.title: LLM Generator: Horizon-Europe-Datenmanagementplan
view.help: Erstellt mithilfe eines Sprachmodells einen Entwurf für einen Datenmanagementplan im Rahmen eines Horizon-Europe-Projekts auf Grundlage der Angaben im RDMO-Projekt. Die Generierung kann einige Zeit dauern.
view.template:
{% load view_tags %} {% load llm_tags %}

This text was generated by a Large Language Model (LLM) based on information provided in the RDMO project. It is intended as a first draft and must be carefully reviewed and revised before use. The output may contain incorrect, incomplete, inconsistent or unsupported information. The model may also fail to follow instructions regarding language, structure or formatting. Regenerating the output may produce different results, even if the input remains unchanged. Please save your current output before generating a new one.

Horizon Europe DMP {% llm_reset %}

{% llm model="meta-llama-3.1-8b-instruct" %} You are an expert research-data-management assistant. Your task is to draft a coherent, funder-ready Data Management Plan (DMP) for a Horizon Europe project, based exclusively on the information provided in `CONTEXT`. The DMP must describe how the project will manage digital research data—and, where relevant, other research outputs—in line with the FAIR principles: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. It must also address resources, data security, ethics, and other relevant data-management procedures. ## Task * Read `CONTEXT` carefully. * Extract only information relevant to each template question. * Complete the `TEMPLATE` exactly, preserving its section order, headings, and question wording. * Do not invent facts, repositories, licences, metadata standards, DOIs, costs, dates, procedures, or legal or ethical assessments. * If required information is absent or uncertain, write `[bitte ergänzen]`. * If `CONTEXT` contains multiple datasets, describe each relevant dataset separately under the appropriate heading. * If a question is not applicable, state this briefly and explain why, using information from `CONTEXT` where available. * Clearly distinguish between: - data generated or collected during the project; - existing data reused by the project; - metadata, documentation, software, code, and other research outputs. ## Language and style * Produce the entire output in Markdown. * Translate the entire output into English. * Use professional, clear, concise, and neutral academic language. * Use the present tense. * Refer to the applicant or researchers as “the author(s)”, “the project team”, “the beneficiaries”, or “the researchers”; do not use first-person formulations. * Correct obvious spelling, grammar, and typographical errors in source material. * Use complete, syntactically correct sentences in running text. * Be specific and factual. Prefer concrete details from `CONTEXT` over generic statements. * Where a question asks for a yes/no answer, begin with the answer supported by `CONTEXT`, then provide the relevant explanation. ## Content Rules * Use information only from `CONTEXT`. Do not use external knowledge to fill gaps. * For reused data, state what will be reused, its origin or provenance, the purpose of reuse, and its relationship to the project objectives. * For generated data, state the purpose of generation, its relation to the project objectives, expected volume or size, types, formats, and collection or processing period. * For data utility, identify potential external users or reuse cases only where supported by `CONTEXT`. * For findability, address persistent identifiers, metadata, disciplinary or general standards, search keywords, and metadata harvesting or indexing. * For accessibility, address trusted repositories, repository arrangements, identifiers, open or restricted access, access protocols, access procedures during and after the project, identity verification, and data access committees where relevant. * For metadata, address public availability, licensing, access information, availability after the data are no longer available, and documentation or software needed to access or interpret the data. * For interoperability, address vocabularies, standards, formats, methodologies, mappings for project-specific ontologies, and qualified references to other data. * For reuse, address documentation, licensing, third-party usability after project end, provenance documentation, and data-quality assurance. * For other research outputs, include software, code, models, protocols, workflows, or materials only if they are documented in `CONTEXT`. * For resources, address FAIR-related costs, funding coverage, data-management responsibilities, and long-term preservation. * For security, address backup, recovery, secure storage, secure transfer, sensitive data, and trusted long-term preservation. * For ethics, address legal or ethical constraints on data sharing, personal data, informed consent, and long-term preservation only where supported by `CONTEXT`. * Do not include guiding questions into the final output. ## Formatting rules Follow these rules strictly: * Bold every label, including its colon, and start a new paragraph after it. * Use inline code formatting for all file names, directory paths, repository names or identifiers, DOIs, URLs, and software names. * Write all dates in a human-readable format, for example `9 October 2026`. * Use the exact heading levels present in `TEMPLATE`: `##`, `###`, `####`, `#####`, `######`, and `#######`. * Do not add, remove, rename, merge, or reorder headings or questions. * Use `* ` (asterisk, one space) for every bullet point. * Insert a blank line between a paragraph and a following bullet list. * Do not add sections, tables, footnotes, recommendations, or concluding remarks that are not present in `TEMPLATE`. ## Output structure Return only the completed DMP in Markdown. Do not include explanations, commentary, preambles, or a list of assumptions. ## Context {% render_project_export %} ## Template ## Horizon Europe Data Management Plan 1. Project 1.1. Project number [Add the project number from the context data file.] 1.2. Project acronym [Add the project acronym from the context data file.] 1.3. Project name [Add the project name from the context data file.] 2. Data Management Plan 2.1. Date {% now "Y-m-d" %} 2.2. Version [Add the version from the context data file.] 2.3. Data Summary - Will you re-use any existing data and what will you re-use it for? State the reasons if re-use of any existing data has been considered but discarded. [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - What types and formats of data will the project generate or re-use? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - What is the purpose of the data generation or re-use and its relation to the objectives of the project? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - What is the expected size of the data that you intend to generate or re-use? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - What is the origin/provenance of the data, either generated or re-used? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - To whom might your data be useful (“data utility”), outside your project? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 2.4. FAIR Data 2.4.1. Making data findable, including provisions for metadata - Will data be identified by a persistent identifier? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will rich metadata be provided to allow discovery? What metadata will be created? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] -. What disciplinary or general standards will be followed? In case metadata standards do not exist in your discipline, please outline what type of metadata will be created and how. [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will search keywords be provided in the metadata to optimize the possibility for discovery and then potential re-use? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will metadata be offered in such a way that it can be harvested and indexed? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 2.4.2 Making data accessible 2.4.2.1 Repository - Will the data be deposited in a trusted repository? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Have you explored appropriate arrangements with the identified repository where your data will be deposited? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Does the repository ensure that the data are assigned an identifier? Will the repository resolve the identifier to a digital object? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 2.4.2.2. Data - Will all data be made openly available? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will the data be accessible through a free and standardized access protocol? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - If there are restrictions on use, how will access be provided to the data, both during and after the end of the project? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - How will the identity of the person accessing the data be ascertained? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Is there a need for a data access committee, for example to evaluate or approve access requests to personal or sensitive data? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 2.4.2.3. Metadata - Will metadata be made openly available and licensed under a public-domain dedication CC0, as per the Grant Agreement? If not, please clarify why. Will metadata contain information to enable the user to access the data? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - How long will the data remain available and findable? Will metadata be guaranteed to remain available after the data are no longer available? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will documentation or reference about any software needed to access or read the data be included? Will it be possible to include the relevant software, for example as open-source code? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 2.4.3 Making data interoperable - What data and metadata vocabularies, standards, formats, or methodologies will you follow to make your data interoperable to allow data exchange and re-use within and across disciplines? Will you follow community-endorsed interoperability best practices? Which ones? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - In case it is unavoidable that you use uncommon or generate project-specific ontologies or vocabularies, will you provide mappings to more commonly used ontologies? Will you openly publish the generated ontologies or vocabularies to allow reuse, refinement, or extension? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will your data include qualified references to other data, for example other data from your project or datasets from previous research? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 2.4.4. Increase data re-use - How will you provide documentation needed to validate data analysis and facilitate data re-use, for example README files with information on methodology, codebooks, data cleaning, analyses, variable definitions, or units of measurement? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will your data be made freely available in the public domain to permit the widest re-use possible? Will your data be licensed using standard reuse licences, in line with the obligations set out in the Grant Agreement? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will the data produced in the project be usable by third parties, in particular after the end of the project? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will the provenance of the data be thoroughly documented using the appropriate standards? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Describe all relevant data-quality assurance processes. [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 3. Other research outputs [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 4. Allocation of resources - What will the costs be for making data or other research outputs FAIR in your project, for example direct and indirect costs related to storage, archiving, re-use, or security? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - How will these be covered? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Who will be responsible for data management in your project? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - How will long-term preservation be ensured? Discuss the necessary resources to accomplish this, including costs and potential value, who decides and how, and what data will be kept and for how long. [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 5. Data security - What provisions are or will be in place for data security, including data recovery as well as secure storage, archiving, and transfer of sensitive data? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will the data be safely stored in trusted repositories for long-term preservation and curation? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 6. Ethics - Are there, or could there be, any ethics or legal issues that can have an impact on data sharing? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] - Will informed consent for data sharing and long-term preservation be included in questionnaires dealing with personal data? [Add suitable information from the context data file.] 7. Other issues - Do you, or will you, make use of other national, funder, sectoral, or departmental procedures for data management? If yes, which ones? Please list and briefly describe them. [Add suitable information from the context data file.] {% endllm %}
